entry.title: RoboArchitect: Automating the Design of Robotic Agents with Persistent Memory
entry.summary:
Recent work shows that a frozen robot policy performs far better inside an agent harness, where control code decides when to query the policy, consult vision tools, or command the arm directly. Yet today these harnesses are built by hand and redesigned for each new robot or benchmark. We show that harness design can be automated, offering a strong alternative to finetuning on a novel setup.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents #robotics

entry.title: CEPO: A General Framework for Improving Prompt Optimization in Multi-Agent Systems
entry.summary:
Multi-agent systems (MAS) require both effective coordination and specialized task execution. Existing prompt optimization approaches typically couple these functions within agent-specific prompts. We introduce Coordinator-Executor Prompt Optimization (CEPO), a general framework for improving prompt optimization in MAS.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents

entry.title: REA: A Routed Embodied Agent Runtime for Asynchronous Brain-Cerebellum Control
entry.summary:
Foundation models are becoming remarkably reliable at high-level reasoning, yet they remain too slow and costly to serve as fine-grained controllers. Conversely, fast policies like VLAs and whole-body controllers offer more efficient reflexes, but struggle to generalize. While pairing a deliberative brain (foundation models) with a reactive cerebellum (fast policies) seems natural for embodied systems, two obstacles remain: methods are built and scored on incompatible stacks, and their asynchronous coordination is difficult.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents #robotics

entry.title: CaPtain: A Pipeline for Post-Training Code-as-Policy Robot Agents
entry.summary:
Across coding, web, and tool-use tasks, language-model agents are now routinely trained with the same recipe: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to learn the interface, then multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) to master it. Code-as-policy (CaP) casts robot manipulation in the same form, as the policy writes code against robot APIs and reads back the results, so the same recipe should apply. Yet existing CaP agents sidestep training: they either prompt closed frontier models or delegate manipulation to pre-trained vision-language-action models (VLAs) and high-level skills, while small open vision-language models (VLMs) fail outright.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents #robotics

entry.title: How Much Can Tool Calls Reveal About You? Privacy Leakage from Tool-Call Traces
entry.summary:
Large language model (LLM)-based agents interact with external tools through protocols such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP), producing tool-call traces that may expose behavioral signals about users. In this work, we systematically study the risk of user-profile inference from MCP tool-call traces, where observers infer user attributes from protocol-valid tool interactions without access to user conversations. We introduce PrivacyTrace, a benchmark containing 1,000 synthetic user profiles and 4,000 agent trajectories across four domains, generated with real MCP tools from 25 servers.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #llm #agents

entry.title: Fuzzers vs. AI: Comparing Fuzzilli and BigSleep on JavaScript Engines
entry.summary:
Summary Project Zero compared two automated tools used by Google to find vulnerabilities in Chrome’s JavaScript engine, V8, on a regular basis. Fuzzilli is a generative JavaScript engine fuzzer and BigSleep is an LLM-based bug finding system. In the past six months, BigSleep found more vulnerabilities than Fuzzilli (45 versus 37) with a 25% overlap in the specific bugs reported.

Source: Google Project Zero · Tags: #infosec #kernel-os #agents

entry.title: Strategic Tanking in Stable Matching Markets
entry.summary:
Motivated by a broad literature in psychology, organizational behavior, and matching markets, we introduce strategic tanking: an agent deliberately makes themselves less attractive to selected potential partners in order to improve their eventual assignment. Unlike traditional manipulation in stable matching, a tanker does not misreport whom they prefer; instead, they influence how others rank them. We show that tanking has a striking connection to classical preference manipulation.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #agents

entry.title: Truthful and Admissible Principal--Agent Testing with Nuisance Parameters
entry.summary:
Statistical contracts reward experimenters according to the evidence produced by a costly study, so the reward rule influences both who participates and what they report. Principal--agent testing theory explains how to prevent ineffective proposals from being profitable. We ask when such contracts can also elicit honest parameter reports if the decision concerns a mean effect but the variance or distributional shape is unknown.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #probability-stats #agents

entry.title: Optic flow in the visual system determines interaction force and collective motion
entry.summary:
Collective motion in animal groups relies on visual cues, yet how individual sensory inputs translate into group-level dynamics remains unclear. Traditional models often assume pre-defined ``3A" rules - avoidance, attraction, and alignment - which require agents to directly access the exact positions and velocities of their neighbors. Here, we propose a minimal model based on fundamental visual processing shared across species: detection of image size and optic flow.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #agents
